Pagogo (Japanese: パゴゴ Pagogo) is a , a Legendary Pokémon featured prominently in . It is Rystal's only known Pokémon and the first that Liko in the land of Kitakami, as well as her third overall. It was seen most of the time outside its .

==In animation==
===History===
====Pre-series====
 ]]
=====With Rystal=====
100 years prior to the events of , Rystal found a during a trip to the Great Crater of Paldea and nicknamed it Pagogo. One day, she was running away from a group of thieves who wanted to steal Pagogo, but they were saved by Lucius, who scared the thieves away with his Black Rayquaza. Since then, Rystal and Pagogo accompanied Lucius in his journey, as he caught the remaining members of the Six Heroes and sought the Pokémon paradise known as Laqua. At some point, they were joined by Gibeon and his White Zygarde.
 sealing the Laquium away]]
Finally having reached Laqua, the trio, now known as the Explorers, found themselves in trouble after Gibeon meddled with the Laquium crystals found in the paradise, causing them to spread uncontrollably and making wild Pokémon go feral. Upon witnessing its Trainer's determination, Pagogo transformed into its and gave some of its energy to the Six Heroes, allowing them to seal the Laquium away. In the aftermath, Lucius was trapped in Laqua, the Six Heroes got scattered around the , and Pagogo fell into a deep sleep in its dormant, jewel-like state.

Rystal chose to wear the dormant Pagogo around her neck in the form of a pendant ever since, hoping it'd awaken someday. After she passed away, her pendant was left inside a briefcase in the attic of her daughter's home, alongside Lucius's diary.

=====With Diana=====
 finding Terapagos in the form of a pendant]]
Many years later, the pendant and Lucius's diary were found by Rystal's granddaughter, Diana, when she was a young girl. The tales of the Ancient Adventurer motivated her to begin a journey, hoping to find out if the stories were true, and she took the pendant with her, unaware that it was a Pokémon. Despite her many adventures, Terapagos never once showed signals of a reawakening.

A year prior to the events of the series, Diana gifted the pendant to her granddaughter, Liko, telling her that it would become important to her in the future. Some time after this, she learned about the Explorers, a suspicious organization that wanted the pendant for an unknown purpose. Fearing for her granddaughter's safety, she, through Lucca, enlisted the help of the Rising Volt Tacklers to protect her.

==== ====
=====As a wild Pokémon=====
 for the first time]]
Terapagos debuted in The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), first appearing in its dormant state. During a school break, Liko was approached by Amethio, who claimed he was sent by her grandmother to retrieve and return the pendant to her. Finding the situation suspicious, Liko instead took the pendant and fled her dormitory. She eventually got cornered by Amethio and his subordinates, Zirc and Onia, but in the right moment, Friede swoop in from above. While Friede's Charizard battled Amethio's Ceruledge, Liko took the opportunity to escape just as a stray flew towards her. The pendant glowed and created an energy barrier, protecting Liko and her from harm. Inside the barrier, Liko briefly saw, though not recognized, Terapagos in its Normal Form before it reverted back into a pendant.

In The Treasure After the Storm!, Liko's pendant seemed to resonate with Roy's Ancient Poké Ball as they were being chased by a group of wild Pokémon. In The Ancient Poké Ball, the pendant once again activated, creating another barrier to protect its owner from imminent danger and later, during another situation of distress, resonating with the Ancient Poké Ball, which then opened, releasing the Black Rayquaza. Intrigued, Liko decided to continue looking into her pendant's mystery as the Rising Volt Tacklers traveled to Paldea.

In The Future I Choose, after helping restore the forest where it lived, Liko's pendant began to glow and transformed back into Terapagos, which caused Arboliva to share a vision of a mysterious man to the group. After the vision was shown, Terapagos reverted back to its dormant state and Arboliva returned to its Ancient Poké Ball, allowing Liko to take it under her care. Afterward, Liko decided she wanted to see her grandmother to learn more about the pendant. 

In Fly! Wattrel!!, Liko was lured away from the Rising Volt Tacklers by Spinel, who then used his to erase her memories and easily steal her pendant. The pendant remained under Spinel's possession until Quaxly, We Can Do It, where Liko, Roy, and Dot challenged him to a battle. Spinel, commanding his Pokémon remotely from a hidden location, quickly overwhelmed them once he was up to his final Pokémon, . Their desire to retrieve the pendant caused it to glow brightly, revealing where Spinel was hiding and allowing Sprigatito to retrieve it.
 ]]
In Charge! Galar Mine!, the group encountered a that had an Ancient Poké Ball, indicating that it had belonged to the Ancient Adventurer Lucius just like Arboliva. However, they were forced to retreat after Moltres had defeated them and injured Captain Pikachu. In the following episode, Liko and Roy returned to the Galar Mine and battled the Malevolent Pokémon in an attempt to calm it down. After successfully calming Moltres down with Sprigatito's aromatic , Liko's pendant started to glow and transformed into Terapagos. It began to communicate with Moltres, after which it returned to its Ancient Poké Ball and allowed Liko to take it under her care. After this point, Terapagos no longer reverted to its dormant state inside the pendant, instead choosing to remain awakened to travel alongside Liko. This was noticed by Amethio, who would tell his teammates that they planned to steal the mysterious Pokémon.

In Roar of the Black Rayquaza, as the Black Rayquaza appeared before the Rising Volt Tacklers and easily defeated Amethio, Terapagos transformed into its to protect its friends, having its clash with Rayquaza's . After that, however, it passed out from exhaustion and Rayquaza left. Friede and Diana later theorized that Rayquaza was only testing Terapagos, who had just awakened some of its powers after three of the Six Heroes had been gathered.
 
During Liko's time as a Naranja Academy student, from Welcome to Naranja Academy! to Shine on, Terastallization! Liko vs. Roy!, Terapagos was usually seen traveling inside her bag.

In The Terapagos I Don't Know, knowing about Terapagos sightings in Paldea through old records, Liko, Roy, Dot, and Friede visited Clavell and Geeta hoping they'd know something about them. They revealed old sketches of Terapagos's Normal and Terastal Forms, claiming it possessed a strong connection to the Terastal phenomenon and that it was once sighted within the Great Crater of Paldea, in Area Zero, which was recorded in the Scarlet Book, supposedly in its third form. Later on, during their travels with Raifort, Terapagos quickly striked a friendship with a wild .

In The Approaching Shadow!, after an encounter with Amethio on Glaseado Mountain, Liko was forced to battle him in order to keep Terapagos safe. They were interrupted by Spinel, who revealed he came into possession of a shard of Laquium, which he used to power up his . Infuriated by this, Terapagos changed into its Terastal Form, purified Umbreon of the Laquium's effect, and destroyed the shard before falling unconscious. Terapagos later awakened inside a cave that Spinel trapped it, Liko, and Amethio inside of. Despite Amethio's insistence that capturing it was the last thing on his mind at the moment, Terapagos ignored his words and angrily yelled at him.

In Encounters at the Crystal Pool, at Briar's suggestion, the Rising Volt Tacklers went to the Crystal Pool so Terapagos could attempt to communicate with Lucius by using the site's rumored ability to summon the deceased. Despite its best efforts, Terapagos was unable to call on Lucius's spirit.
 
In The Three Explorers, after learning about the existence of Rystal, the Rising Volt Tacklers traveled to the Crystal Pool once more and had Terapagos try and call on the spirit of Rystal this time. This attempt was successful, allowing them to meet Terapagos's former Trainer, as well as her child, . In the next episode, after Rystal had told them the original Explorers' journey to Laqua, she returned to her original time, though not before asking Liko to take care of her former partner, filling Terapagos with sadness. After being given a by Friede, Liko Terapagos, formally adding it to her team, and started using the nickname Rystal once gave it: Pagogo.

=====With Liko=====
 
After the Rising Volt Tacklers managed to convince Lucius's Gouging Fire to join them in The Pillar of Fire, Pagogo and the gathered heroes summoned the Black Rayquaza to Area Zero for one final challenge, which took place in the following episode. Eventually, when all of the Rising Volt Tacklers' Pokémon except for Roy's Crocalor had been defeated, Pagogo transformed into its Terastal Form and decided to join the fray. Their collective efforts kept Rayquaza on the defensive, allowing Pagogo to strike it with a powerful Tera Starstorm, though not without being hit hard by a in the process. Then, it chose to use the last of its remaining strength to Terastallize Crocalor, giving him the power boost necessary to damage Rayquaza enough for Roy to recall it into its Ancient Poké Ball. Now, with all Six Heroes gathered, Pagogo fully regained its full strength.

Led by the Black Rayquaza, the Rising Volt Tackles arrived at Mount Pericarp in Where the Land Meets the Sky. At various points during their trek up the mountain, Pagogo summoned one of the Six Heroes to aid the group, allowing them to climb higher, cross waters, and overcome obstacles in order to reach Laqua. The group then went further into the paradise's forest in the following episode, finally finding the area that had been sealed away 100 years ago. Realizing the barrier was still up, Liko had Pagogo transform into its Terastal Form and remove it, but this left it exhausted in the process, forcing her to recall it for the time being. This, however, did not last long, as Pagogo forced itself out of its Poké Ball just as Gibeon began meddling with the Laquium crystals again.
 
In Guided by the Black Rayquaza!, the group eventually reached Gibeon and the White Zygarde, who was digging up a Laquium cluster. At that moment, Pagogo summoned the Six Heroes, and they collectively witnessed as Lucius emerged alive from the crystals. After reuniting, Pagogo lent some of its power to Lucius in order for him to explain everything. Now with the knowledge that only sealing the Laquium away won't be effective, it transformed into its Terastal Form and gathered the Six Heroes' powers into itself while the group proved themselves to the White Zygarde. Once it was ready, in Where the Adventure Leads, Pagogo Terastallized, changing into its Stellar Form, and purified the Laquium with the help of the Six Heroes. It instantly returned to its Normal Form afterwards and bid farewell to Lucius, who, like Gibeon, was only being kept alive due to Laquium. Before parting, the Ancient Adventurer entrusted Pagogo's safety to Liko.
 
Over the year following the events at Laqua, Pagogo did not come out from its Poké Ball, seemingly hibernating just as it did 100 years ago. In Following Traces of Laquium, it finally reawakened in order to shield Liko from a caused by two rampaging that had been affected by Laquium. Pagogo transformed into its Terastal Form and purified the Laquium affecting the Steelix, clearing the ill effects. From here onwards, in the event of the group finding a Laquium Sign, they would work to subdue the afflicted Pokémon, allowing Pagogo, in its battle form, to cure it from the substance's effects.

In Reunion in Cortondo, Pagogo was chosen by Katy to be Liko's Pokémon for their official rematch, facing off against her . Its brute force and resilience proved to be a tough match, but Pagogo was able to overcome it with a Tera Starstorm in the end, even after Ursaring had Terastallized, winning Liko the battle.

In The Knight in the Ruins, Pagogo reunited with the Charcadet it had met a year back in some Paldean ruins. After 's was discovered to be on a Laquium-induced rampage, it helped Charcadet in subduing the Spicy Pepper Pokémon. Later, as Liko was about to bid farewell to Charcadet, Pagogo encouraged it to join them.

In The Six Heroes Unleashed!, Pagogo was used alongside the rest of Liko, Roy, and Ult's Pokémon to battle against five of the Six Heroes, who were under the influence of the Super Strong Spheres. Overwhelmed by the opponents, Liko quickly had Pagogo purify the Laquium from the heroes' bodies, but the Explorers used the Super Strong Spheres once more on them. This time, aimed directly at Pagogo, knocking out both it and , who had jumped in to try and defend it.
 
In The Catcher in the Sky, Pagogo used its in an attempt to catch Friede, whose spaceship was about to crash-land into the ground. Several of the other Rising Volt Tacklers' Pokémon used their moves to support Pagogo, but Friede's ship was deflected off the barrier. Pagogo then used its power to Terastallize Captain Pikachu into a , which allowed Captain Pikachu to safely return Friede to the Brave Olivine.

In HZ125, Pagogo teamed up with Zygarde to help the remaining Six Heroes regain the memories of their adventures with Lucius, Rystal, Gibeon, and the Rising Volt Tacklers. Pagogo then Terastalized all the remaining Six Heroes to remove the effects of Laquium from them.

After training and returning to Laqua, Pagogo and the representatives of each Tera Type began to purify the Laquium Core in HZ135, but the Explorers interfered and caused Penny's to faint. The purification attempt went awry for a moment, but stabilized once Coral volunteered her , Screamypuff, to take the vacant spot of the Fairy Tera Type. However, they were not able to purify the Core before Spinel merged with it, causing it to awaken and start attacking in retaliation. Dot took notice of its patterns and weak points, and the White Zygarde and Black Rayquaza finally managed to break through its defenses after Mega Evolving in the following episode, allowing Pagogo and the eighteen Tera Type Pokémon to erase the Laquium Core once and for all. With the Laquium threat neutralized, Pagogo chose to remain at Laqua with the Six Heroes and Zygarde to restore the paradise to its previous state. Respecting Pagogo's choice, Liko, Meowscarada, Hatterene, and Armarouge bid it farewell, as they promised to meet it again someday.
 

===Personality and characteristics===
 
Particularly, Pagogo seems to have a special connection to Liko, with her being the first person in generations to be able to reawaken it from its dormant state. It appears to have a strong desire to protect her from harm, which can most notably be seen in The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), Roar of the Black Rayquaza, and Following Traces of Laquium, instances where it reawakened or first transformed into its in order to shield her from imminent danger. It also seems to like sleeping in Liko's backpack and enjoys being held in her arms, as well as in 's. In addition, Pagogo has taken a liking to being inside 's body. Pagogo has been shown to be overall friendly around people and Pokémon alike, having a close bond with the rest of Liko's team, especially with , as Pagogo was the one to encourage it to join her party and is occasionally seen offering it a ride on its back. It maintains its friendship with it after it evolved into . Notable exceptions to Pagogo's friendliness include Amethio, a trait first shown in Reunion at the Ancient Castle! and then again in Liko and Amethio, as it appears to resent the recognition of Amethio's grandfather, Gibeon, in him; and Ult's , due to its constant attempts to eat it.

Pagogo has a strong connection to Lucius, the Six Heroes, and its former Trainer, Rystal, always attempting to call out to them and being extremely happy every time they reunite. Many events of the original Explorers' journey are only revealed to the Rising Volt Tacklers due to Pagogo's ability to share the memories it has from that time. Amongst the Six Heroes, it has the closest bond with Rayquaza, dating back to the day they first met, as depicted in The Wonders of the World!, with Lucius noting that Pagogo was unlike every other Pokémon in that it didn't fear Rayquaza. As seen in The Plan to Capture Rayquaza, Pagogo has the ability to call for the Black Rayquaza with a specific energy signal, which the other Six Heroes seem to share as well, as suggested in The Pillar of Fire. In Respective Departures, Gibeon also claimed that both Pagogo and Rayquaza were the keys to Laqua, in the sense that only the Sky High Pokémon knew the way there and that the Tera Pokémon, with its power fully reawakened, was able to unseal the paradise. Due to their shared history, Pagogo was shown to glow whenever it's near one of the Ancient Poké Balls and is even capable to opening them if necessary, as seen in The Ancient Poké Ball and Where the Land Meets the Sky. It was very happy in Crash! Team Dragon Rampage!, to be reunited with the Black Rayquaza, but upon hearing of the remaining heroes capture by Spinel; Pagogo shared great determination to free them which happened in HZ125. 
 ]]
In Terapagos's Adventure and throughout Terapagos's Exploration Diary, it was shown to have a curious and inquisitive personality, exploring and wandering the Brave Olivine on its own, possibly as a result of being in its dormant form for a very long time. In addition, Pagogo enjoys eating , as they are the only things it will eat; though it has come to enjoy eating other foods, such as sweets.

Although it isn't seen battling much, Pagogo itself is not opposed to the idea, even taking the initiative to do so in Beyond the Shining Rainbow upon sensing Liko's determination. Pagogo's lack of battling appearances could be attributed to its missing powers, as its first battle occurred in Roar of the Black Rayquaza, after three of the Six Heroes had been gathered, and ended with it passing out after a single attack, which meant its power was still incomplete. A similar explanation has been suggested by Diana in Taking the Next Steps as to why the Laquium wasn't completely purified, and that Pagogo in its may need to simultaneously resonate with all eighteen types to be at its strongest; in Don't Give Up, Crocalor!, Briar clarifies that Pagogo needs to resonate with eighteen different Tera Types from Pokémon at the level of the Six Heroes in order to completely purify Laquium.

In The Approaching Shadow!, when Spinel showed a Laquium shard to Pagogo, it became angry and transformed into its , purifying Spinel's of the Laquium's influence and destroying the shard in the process. Spinel came to the conclusion that Pagogo and the Laquium are opposing forces to each other in some fashion. In general, seeing Laquium angers Pagogo. This anger may stem from its first encounter with it alongside the original Explorers in which Lucius was trapped in Laqua, the Six Heroes scattered around world, and itself transformed into a dormant state. Moreover, upon arriving in Laqua and seeing that Gibeon had continued his pursuit of Laquium a hundred years later may have made Pagogo determined not to let what happened to the original Explorers repeat itself with the Rising Volt Tacklers. A year later, Pagogo's anger towards Laquium may have increased further when Spinel used it on the Six Heroes in order to make them to go berserk for his experiments.

==Trivia==
Pagogo's debut in the was the first time that Terapagos was ever shown in its , as it had previously only been revealed in its . It was not identified as Terapagos until the Pokémon Presents, months later. 
In the closed captioning for the TV Tokyo broadcast of HZ023, Terapagos was referred to as コダイカメ Kodaikame (from 古代亀 kodai kame, literally "ancient turtle"). This was later officially confirmed as an error. 
Out of all Pokémon owned by female main characters, Pagogo took the longest to catch after its debut, taking 73 episodes (74 if its first appearance in its pendant form is included).
Pagogo's capture was foreshadowed in Only One Story, where it is seen appearing when Liko sends out her Pokémon.
Pagogo is the first Pokémon owned by a female main character to be:
A Legendary Pokémon.
It was also the first Legendary Pokémon to have been taken in by a female main character since took in Squishy in From A to Z!, 362 episodes earlier.
An officially owned single-stage Pokémon since caught her in Emolga the Irresistible!, 626 episodes earlier.
Officially without recatching it later, excluding temporary Pokémon, since released her in A Togepi Mirage!, 1,049 episodes earlier.
Pagogo was the only Pokémon owned by Liko that:
Is not part of an evolutionary line.
Is a Legendary Pokémon.
Has multiple forms.
Has a nickname.
Is not a dual-type Pokémon.
Pagogo was the only single-type Pokémon owned by the younger members of the Rising Volt Tacklers.
In Encounters at the Crystal Pool, a appeared in Area Zero during a flashback; however, it is unknown whether the Terapagos in question was Pagogo or another Terapagos.
In its , Pagogo is animated with 3D animation rather than 2D, similar to in the same series and in .
Additionally, when Terapagos transformed into its Stellar Form for the first time in The Wonders of the World!, its body was coated in a light blue glow, which hid its design's details. This was probably done to hide the form until it appeared in the present in The Earthshaking White Zygarde.
Unlike the dormant state of the from The Indigo Disk expansion of , Pagogo's star at the tip of its tail is still seen sticking out. Pagogo's shell also shrinks to a much smaller size in its dormant state whereas the Terapagos in the games stays roughly the same size.
In the Brazilian Portuguese dub, Pagogo is referred to as male.

sections.heading: With Liko
sections.text:
After the Rising Volt Tacklers managed to convince Lucius's Gouging Fire to join them in The Pillar of Fire, Pagogo and the gathered heroes summoned the Black Rayquaza to Area Zero for one final challenge, which took place in the following episode. Eventually, when all of the Rising Volt Tacklers' Pokémon except for Roy's Crocalor had been defeated, Pagogo transformed into its Terastal Form and decided to join the fray. Their collective efforts kept Rayquaza on the defensive, allowing Pagogo to strike it with a powerful Tera Starstorm, though not without being hit hard by a in the process. Then, it chose to use the last of its remaining strength to Terastallize Crocalor, giving him the power boost necessary to damage Rayquaza enough for Roy to recall it into its Ancient Poké Ball. Now, with all Six Heroes gathered, Pagogo fully regained its full strength.

Led by the Black Rayquaza, the Rising Volt Tackles arrived at Mount Pericarp in Where the Land Meets the Sky. At various points during their trek up the mountain, Pagogo summoned one of the Six Heroes to aid the group, allowing them to climb higher, cross waters, and overcome obstacles in order to reach Laqua. The group then went further into the paradise's forest in the following episode, finally finding the area that had been sealed away 100 years ago. Realizing the barrier was still up, Liko had Pagogo transform into its Terastal Form and remove it, but this left it exhausted in the process, forcing her to recall it for the time being. This, however, did not last long, as Pagogo forced itself out of its Poké Ball just as Gibeon began meddling with the Laquium crystals again.
 
In Guided by the Black Rayquaza!, the group eventually reached Gibeon and the White Zygarde, who was digging up a Laquium cluster. At that moment, Pagogo summoned the Six Heroes, and they collectively witnessed as Lucius emerged alive from the crystals. After reuniting, Pagogo lent some of its power to Lucius in order for him to explain everything. Now with the knowledge that only sealing the Laquium away won't be effective, it transformed into its Terastal Form and gathered the Six Heroes' powers into itself while the group proved themselves to the White Zygarde. Once it was ready, in Where the Adventure Leads, Pagogo Terastallized, changing into its Stellar Form, and purified the Laquium with the help of the Six Heroes. It instantly returned to its Normal Form afterwards and bid farewell to Lucius, who, like Gibeon, was only being kept alive due to Laquium. Before parting, the Ancient Adventurer entrusted Pagogo's safety to Liko.
 
Over the year following the events at Laqua, Pagogo did not come out from its Poké Ball, seemingly hibernating just as it did 100 years ago. In Following Traces of Laquium, it finally reawakened in order to shield Liko from a caused by two rampaging that had been affected by Laquium. Pagogo transformed into its Terastal Form and purified the Laquium affecting the Steelix, clearing the ill effects. From here onwards, in the event of the group finding a Laquium Sign, they would work to subdue the afflicted Pokémon, allowing Pagogo, in its battle form, to cure it from the substance's effects.

In Reunion in Cortondo, Pagogo was chosen by Katy to be Liko's Pokémon for their official rematch, facing off against her . Its brute force and resilience proved to be a tough match, but Pagogo was able to overcome it with a Tera Starstorm in the end, even after Ursaring had Terastallized, winning Liko the battle.

In The Knight in the Ruins, Pagogo reunited with the Charcadet it had met a year back in some Paldean ruins. After 's was discovered to be on a Laquium-induced rampage, it helped Charcadet in subduing the Spicy Pepper Pokémon. Later, as Liko was about to bid farewell to Charcadet, Pagogo encouraged it to join them.

In The Six Heroes Unleashed!, Pagogo was used alongside the rest of Liko, Roy, and Ult's Pokémon to battle against five of the Six Heroes, who were under the influence of the Super Strong Spheres. Overwhelmed by the opponents, Liko quickly had Pagogo purify the Laquium from the heroes' bodies, but the Explorers used the Super Strong Spheres once more on them. This time, aimed directly at Pagogo, knocking out both it and , who had jumped in to try and defend it.
 
In The Catcher in the Sky, Pagogo used its in an attempt to catch Friede, whose spaceship was about to crash-land into the ground. Several of the other Rising Volt Tacklers' Pokémon used their moves to support Pagogo, but Friede's ship was deflected off the barrier. Pagogo then used its power to Terastallize Captain Pikachu into a , which allowed Captain Pikachu to safely return Friede to the Brave Olivine.

In HZ125, Pagogo teamed up with Zygarde to help the remaining Six Heroes regain the memories of their adventures with Lucius, Rystal, Gibeon, and the Rising Volt Tacklers. Pagogo then Terastalized all the remaining Six Heroes to remove the effects of Laquium from them.

After training and returning to Laqua, Pagogo and the representatives of each Tera Type began to purify the Laquium Core in HZ135, but the Explorers interfered and caused Penny's to faint. The purification attempt went awry for a moment, but stabilized once Coral volunteered her , Screamypuff, to take the vacant spot of the Fairy Tera Type. However, they were not able to purify the Core before Spinel merged with it, causing it to awaken and start attacking in retaliation. Dot took notice of its patterns and weak points, and the White Zygarde and Black Rayquaza finally managed to break through its defenses after Mega Evolving in the following episode, allowing Pagogo and the eighteen Tera Type Pokémon to erase the Laquium Core once and for all. With the Laquium threat neutralized, Pagogo chose to remain at Laqua with the Six Heroes and Zygarde to restore the paradise to its previous state. Respecting Pagogo's choice, Liko, Meowscarada, Hatterene, and Armarouge bid it farewell, as they promised to meet it again someday.

sections.heading: Personality and characteristics
sections.text:
Particularly, Pagogo seems to have a special connection to Liko, with her being the first person in generations to be able to reawaken it from its dormant state. It appears to have a strong desire to protect her from harm, which can most notably be seen in The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), Roar of the Black Rayquaza, and Following Traces of Laquium, instances where it reawakened or first transformed into its in order to shield her from imminent danger. It also seems to like sleeping in Liko's backpack and enjoys being held in her arms, as well as in 's. In addition, Pagogo has taken a liking to being inside 's body. Pagogo has been shown to be overall friendly around people and Pokémon alike, having a close bond with the rest of Liko's team, especially with , as Pagogo was the one to encourage it to join her party and is occasionally seen offering it a ride on its back. It maintains its friendship with it after it evolved into . Notable exceptions to Pagogo's friendliness include Amethio, a trait first shown in Reunion at the Ancient Castle! and then again in Liko and Amethio, as it appears to resent the recognition of Amethio's grandfather, Gibeon, in him; and Ult's , due to its constant attempts to eat it.

Pagogo has a strong connection to Lucius, the Six Heroes, and its former Trainer, Rystal, always attempting to call out to them and being extremely happy every time they reunite. Many events of the original Explorers' journey are only revealed to the Rising Volt Tacklers due to Pagogo's ability to share the memories it has from that time. Amongst the Six Heroes, it has the closest bond with Rayquaza, dating back to the day they first met, as depicted in The Wonders of the World!, with Lucius noting that Pagogo was unlike every other Pokémon in that it didn't fear Rayquaza. As seen in The Plan to Capture Rayquaza, Pagogo has the ability to call for the Black Rayquaza with a specific energy signal, which the other Six Heroes seem to share as well, as suggested in The Pillar of Fire. In Respective Departures, Gibeon also claimed that both Pagogo and Rayquaza were the keys to Laqua, in the sense that only the Sky High Pokémon knew the way there and that the Tera Pokémon, with its power fully reawakened, was able to unseal the paradise. Due to their shared history, Pagogo was shown to glow whenever it's near one of the Ancient Poké Balls and is even capable to opening them if necessary, as seen in The Ancient Poké Ball and Where the Land Meets the Sky. It was very happy in Crash! Team Dragon Rampage!, to be reunited with the Black Rayquaza, but upon hearing of the remaining heroes capture by Spinel; Pagogo shared great determination to free them which happened in HZ125. 
 ]]
In Terapagos's Adventure and throughout Terapagos's Exploration Diary, it was shown to have a curious and inquisitive personality, exploring and wandering the Brave Olivine on its own, possibly as a result of being in its dormant form for a very long time. In addition, Pagogo enjoys eating , as they are the only things it will eat; though it has come to enjoy eating other foods, such as sweets.

Although it isn't seen battling much, Pagogo itself is not opposed to the idea, even taking the initiative to do so in Beyond the Shining Rainbow upon sensing Liko's determination. Pagogo's lack of battling appearances could be attributed to its missing powers, as its first battle occurred in Roar of the Black Rayquaza, after three of the Six Heroes had been gathered, and ended with it passing out after a single attack, which meant its power was still incomplete. A similar explanation has been suggested by Diana in Taking the Next Steps as to why the Laquium wasn't completely purified, and that Pagogo in its may need to simultaneously resonate with all eighteen types to be at its strongest; in Don't Give Up, Crocalor!, Briar clarifies that Pagogo needs to resonate with eighteen different Tera Types from Pokémon at the level of the Six Heroes in order to completely purify Laquium.

In The Approaching Shadow!, when Spinel showed a Laquium shard to Pagogo, it became angry and transformed into its , purifying Spinel's of the Laquium's influence and destroying the shard in the process. Spinel came to the conclusion that Pagogo and the Laquium are opposing forces to each other in some fashion. In general, seeing Laquium angers Pagogo. This anger may stem from its first encounter with it alongside the original Explorers in which Lucius was trapped in Laqua, the Six Heroes scattered around world, and itself transformed into a dormant state. Moreover, upon arriving in Laqua and seeing that Gibeon had continued his pursuit of Laquium a hundred years later may have made Pagogo determined not to let what happened to the original Explorers repeat itself with the Rising Volt Tacklers. A year later, Pagogo's anger towards Laquium may have increased further when Spinel used it on the Six Heroes in order to make them to go berserk for his experiments.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
Pagogo's debut in the was the first time that Terapagos was ever shown in its , as it had previously only been revealed in its . It was not identified as Terapagos until the Pokémon Presents, months later. 
In the closed captioning for the TV Tokyo broadcast of HZ023, Terapagos was referred to as コダイカメ Kodaikame (from 古代亀 kodai kame, literally "ancient turtle"). This was later officially confirmed as an error. 
Out of all Pokémon owned by female main characters, Pagogo took the longest to catch after its debut, taking 73 episodes (74 if its first appearance in its pendant form is included).
Pagogo's capture was foreshadowed in Only One Story, where it is seen appearing when Liko sends out her Pokémon.
Pagogo is the first Pokémon owned by a female main character to be:
A Legendary Pokémon.
It was also the first Legendary Pokémon to have been taken in by a female main character since took in Squishy in From A to Z!, 362 episodes earlier.
An officially owned single-stage Pokémon since caught her in Emolga the Irresistible!, 626 episodes earlier.
Officially without recatching it later, excluding temporary Pokémon, since released her in A Togepi Mirage!, 1,049 episodes earlier.
Pagogo was the only Pokémon owned by Liko that:
Is not part of an evolutionary line.
Is a Legendary Pokémon.
Has multiple forms.
Has a nickname.
Is not a dual-type Pokémon.
Pagogo was the only single-type Pokémon owned by the younger members of the Rising Volt Tacklers.
In Encounters at the Crystal Pool, a appeared in Area Zero during a flashback; however, it is unknown whether the Terapagos in question was Pagogo or another Terapagos.
In its , Pagogo is animated with 3D animation rather than 2D, similar to in the same series and in .
Additionally, when Terapagos transformed into its Stellar Form for the first time in The Wonders of the World!, its body was coated in a light blue glow, which hid its design's details. This was probably done to hide the form until it appeared in the present in The Earthshaking White Zygarde.
Unlike the dormant state of the from The Indigo Disk expansion of , Pagogo's star at the tip of its tail is still seen sticking out. Pagogo's shell also shrinks to a much smaller size in its dormant state whereas the Terapagos in the games stays roughly the same size.
In the Brazilian Portuguese dub, Pagogo is referred to as male.
